lines: Reduces damage remaining after block and resistances, before endurance and the rune shield. It absorbs a greater share of smaller hits; armour penetration ignores part of this protection.
new.name: Armour

lines: Reduces damage remaining after rune shield and block. It absorbs a greater share of smaller hits; armour penetration ignores part of this protection.
old.name: Armour

lines: Changes part of one damage type into another before percentage bonuses apply. Converted damage uses the ailments and resistances of its new type and the increases of both its new and its original type, and cannot be converted again; excessive conversion shares are reduced proportionally.
new.name: Damage conversion

lines: Changes part of one damage type into another before percentage bonuses apply. Converted damage uses its new type's bonuses, ailments and resistances and cannot be converted again; excessive conversion shares are reduced proportionally.
old.name: Damage conversion

lines: Workbench crafting makes an item and sets its quality; salvage, runes and the runic anvil then change it. Each item's rarity limits its random affixes.
new.name: Crafting basics

lines: Bleeding, burning and poison deal damage per second for a limited time. Their strength comes from the hit that applied them, with their own increased bonuses and damage over time multipliers on top.
new.name: Damage over time

lines: Defences are armour, evasion rating and rune shield together. An increase to defences applies to all three: it joins each one's own increases in one sum and is not a separate multiplier.
new.name: Defences

lines: The order in which a hit on you is reduced: dodge and evasion, enemy scaling, damage taken, explosion and passive resistances, block, gear resistances, armour, endurance, rune shield, then health.
new.name: Incoming damage calculation

lines: All increased percentages of a number add into one sum; more multipliers each multiply the result. An increase is worth less the more you already have, a more multiplier always keeps its full value.
new.name: Increased and more

lines: Every biome has a level, and so does every creature. Experience fades as you outlevel a biome, while enemy difficulty, stars and modifiers follow the biome and the world's difficulty preset.
new.name: Level scaling

lines: How the damage of one hit is built: base damage, flat damage, conversion and gained-as-extra damage, increased damage, more multipliers, then the critical hit, the target layer and the target's resistances.
new.name: Outgoing damage calculation

lines: Includes slash, pierce and blunt damage. Each type has its own ailment; converted damage keeps growing from the bonuses of its original type as well, while resistances and ailments follow its new type.
new.name: Physical damage

lines: Includes slash, pierce and blunt damage. Each type has its own ailment; converted damage instead uses the bonuses and resistances of its new type.
old.name: Physical damage

lines: Reduces damage of the matching type, up to the limit of 75%. Every source adds to one sum per type: the passive tree, gear, shields while blocking and status effects such as meads and forsaken powers, each showing its number on the thing itself. Resistance above the limit does nothing unless a mastery uses it; resistance penetration can lower effective resistance below zero and increase damage taken.
new.name: Resistances

lines: Reduces damage of the matching type, up to the limit of 75%; resistance above it does nothing unless a mastery uses it. Resistance penetration can lower effective resistance below zero and increase damage taken.
old.name: Resistances

new.name: #% increased defences
#% increased defences

lines: Unbowed Frame: Your constructs cannot lose more than 20% of their health pool to a single hit
new.name: Bound with Iron

lines: Shared Defences: Your constructs inherit your defences: armour, evasion and rune shield
new.name: Barbed Fittings
Constructs: the most of their health pool one hit can take with the mastery option

Living Steel: the most of a living weapon's durability one hit can take (100% = no limit)

Vanilla grades: Resistant gives this many resistance points
Vanilla grades: Slightly resistant gives this many resistance points
Vanilla grades: Very resistant gives this many resistance points
